biggest_catch: Pay and terms are set per listing by individual creators — winning work is competitive and never guaranteed.
catches: Pay, format, and terms are set per listing by each creator — YTJobs publishes no fixed pay range.
Video-production niche only (editors, thumbnail designers, scriptwriters, producers).
Heavy competition from other editors; portfolio quality decides who wins.
Some listings route applications to external forms rather than in-platform apply.

c1.evidence: YTJobs is a live job board on ytjobs.co with fresh, provider-owned listings (a listing crawled hours ago instructs applicants: 'NOTE: We will only be looking at applications applied through YTJobs') — a real, currently-operating deal channel.

c2.evidence: Official pages publish no fixed pay range — pay is set per listing (some listings show salary ranges); framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the platform flow: talent profile, browse listings, apply through YTJobs, hired per listing terms.

c4.evidence: Creating a talent profile and browsing/applying carries no upfront fee.

eligibility: Video editors, thumbnail designers, scriptwriters, and producers who can show portfolio work.
notes: Scenario: video niche (YouTube production). YTJobs is a live job board where YouTube creators post paid editing, design, and production jobs; talent profiles let creators find freelancers. Pay is per-listing and variable — never guaranteed.

steps: Create a YTJobs talent profile with portfolio, skills, niches, and languages.
Browse live job listings for video editors, thumbnail designers, scriptwriters, and producers — or get discovered by hiring creators.
Apply through YTJobs per the listing's instructions (portfolio and turnaround details required).
Get hired and paid per the listing's terms — per project, retainer, or salary.
timing: Listings post continuously; hiring decisions are made per listing by each creator.
